A_target.statement:
Let $f: V \to W$ be a [[Definition:Linear Transformation|linear transformation]].
Then:
:$V / \map \ker f \cong \Img f$
as [[Definition:Vector Space|vector spaces]].

B_source.statement:
Let $f: G \to H$ be a [[Definition:Group Homomorphism|group homomorphism]].
Then:
:$G / \map \ker f \cong \Img f$

validity_conditions: Every subgroup of an abelian group is normal, and a vector space is abelian under addition, so ker(f) automatically yields a well-defined quotient.
The bijective-homomorphism argument transfers verbatim; the extra obligation is checking the induced map respects scalar multiplication.
Rank-nullity is the dimensional shadow of this isomorphism (dim V = dim ker + dim im).
proof_plan: $\map \ker f$ is a [[Definition:Vector Subspace|subspace]], the linear analogue of a [[Definition:Normal Subgroup|normal subgroup]].

Define $\bar f: V / \map \ker f \to \Img f$ by:
:$\map {\bar f} {v + \map \ker f} = \map f v$
The proof of the [[First Isomorphism Theorem for Groups]] applied to $\struct {V, +}$ shows $\bar f$ is well-defined and a [[Definition:Bijection|bijection]].

In addition:
:$\map {\bar f} {\lambda \paren {v + \map \ker f} } = \map f {\lambda v} = \lambda \map f v$
so $\bar f$ is linear, and is an isomorphism of vector spaces.
{{qed}}
